title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political impersonation carried out with generated media. Videos posted to a social platform showed a candidate saying things she never said, and the fabrication was attributed to her directly rather than labelled as satire or simulation. The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the tool produced synthetic speech in a real person's likeness, and it was released to voters under that person's identity.

Catching it would have required the platform or the poster to treat synthetic depictions of a named candidate as a distinct category requiring disclosure. The record here shows no such check. The only corrective action described came from the target's attorneys, after the videos were already public, in the form of a cease-and-desist letter.

What is not established is whether the videos were intended to deceive, whether any legal claim will be filed or succeed, and whether the platform took any action on the posts. A cease-and-desist letter is an allegation, not a finding, and the campaign's dismissal of it is a response, not a defence on the facts.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip from Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and accuses Van Orden of trying to fool voters.

Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring Van Orden's social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he keeps using AI to defame her. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded on social media with another AI-assisted video. Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points in 2024.
